q: For a food processing plant, how much do emissions change if organic waste goes to compost or biogas instead of landfill?
title: Food waste: landfill, compost or biogas
short: A lot. Food waste rotting in a landfill releases methane, so published factors put landfill at several hundred kg CO2e per tonne, while composting and anaerobic digestion sit at roughly ten kg per tonne. Moving most organic waste away from landfill or open dumping is often the biggest single Scope 3 waste cut a food plant can make.
audience: Food processors in India, Vietnam, Indonesia and Turkey

sections.h: Why landfill is so much worse
p: Food waste is mostly carbohydrate, fat and protein. Buried without air, it breaks down over years and releases methane, a gas with a 100 year warming potential of about 27 to 30 times CO2. The IPCC 2006 Guidelines model this with a first order decay method. Composting is aerobic and anaerobic digestion captures the methane as biogas, so both release far less.
The CO2 released from the food itself is biogenic and is not counted in the waste factor; the figures are CO2e because they cover methane and nitrous oxide.

ul: UK DESNZ conversion factors: a waste disposal table with food and drink waste by route (landfill, composting, anaerobic digestion, combustion). Use the current edition.
US EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub and the EPA WARM model as a cross-check.
Factor = tonnes of waste sent by each route x the factor for that route.
p: These factors assume managed landfills, many with some gas capture. Open dumpsites in South Asia and Southeast Asia behave differently: shallow, unmanaged dumps can produce less methane per tonne than a deep landfill, while burning at dumpsites adds other emissions. Say which factor you used and why.

sections.h: Which scope the waste falls in
ul: Waste collected and treated by a third party, including a municipal body or a biogas operator: Scope 3 Category 5, waste generated in operations.
A compost yard or digester you own and run on site: its methane and nitrous oxide are your Scope 1, and the biogenic CO2 is reported separately.
Biogas you burn in place of LPG or furnace oil cuts your Scope 1 fuel use. Count that through lower fuel invoices, not as a negative waste figure.

p: Weighbridge slips or waste contractor invoices showing tonnes by waste type and destination, and the contractor's statement of how the waste is treated. Without tonnes and route, a waste figure is a guess.

example.title: Worked example: 500 tonnes of food waste a year (labelled estimate)
lines: Landfill, illustrative factor 600 kg CO2e per t: 500 x 600 = 300,000 kg, about 300 t CO2e
Composting, illustrative factor 10 kg CO2e per t: 500 x 10 = 5,000 kg, about 5 t CO2e
Difference: 300 t minus 5 t = about 295 t CO2e a year
example.note: Factors are rounded illustrations of the order of the DESNZ values. Use the exact figures from the current edition, and treat results for unmanaged dumpsites as uncertain.

senseible: Senseible keeps waste contractor invoices in the separate Scope 3 evidence trail with the source page and SHA-256 fingerprint. A line gets a figure only when its printed quantity and unit match an approved factor for that category and geography; otherwise it shows Needs Data, with no spend-based fill.
